articles.headline: Watson leads another game-winning drive, Szmyt hits 56-yard FG and Browns beat Steelers 27-24
articles.description: — Deshaun Watson passed for 268 yards and moved the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining that gave Cleveland a 27-24 win over the...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- — Deshaun Watson passed for 268 yards and moved the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining that gave Cleveland a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night.


              Watson, who completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and interception, was 4 of 5 for 46 yards as he led a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter for the third straight week.


              The Browns — who are 3-1 for the first time since 2021 — had a 21-7 lead late in the first half before the Steelers rallied to tie it at 24-all. Aaron Rodgers threw a 3-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth with 1:44 remaining and Rodgers sneaked it in for the 2-point conversion.


              Rodgers, who was 22 of 40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions, had one final chance to get the Steelers in field goal range, but he was picked off by Grant Delpit at the Browns 18 with 1 second left.


              Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries and DK Metcalf had five catches for 115 yards.


              Cleveland's defense sacked Rodgers five times.


              Cleveland has won eight straight Thursday night games, the longest active streak and fourth longest in NFL history. Four have come against the Steelers.


              Pittsburgh (2-2) is 0-10 on the road against AFC North rivals on Thursdays.


              After Cleveland went three-and-out on the opening possession, Pittsburgh went 78 yards in 17 plays, capped by Wilson taking a shovel pass 12 yards around left end on a jet sweep. It was the second straight game in which Steelers have reached the end zone on their first drive.


              The rest of the first half was all Browns. Watson had 181 yards passing by halftime, his most in the first 30 minutes since joining the Browns in 2022.


              Jaleel McLaughlin tied it at 7 with 12:14 remaining in the first half on a 28-yard run around right end. The fourth-year running back broke a pair of tackles at the 22 and went through a narrow opening at the 15 before scoring.


              The drive was set up after Denzel Ward picked off Rodgers' pass intended for Michael Pittman Jr. at the Browns 44 on the second play of the second quarter.


              Cleveland took a 14-7 lead midway through the second quarter on Quinshon Judkins’ 2-yard run off right guard. The touchdown came three plays after Watson found Denzel Boston for a 60-yard completion to the Steelers 14 on the first play of the drive.


              Harold Fannin Jr. then hauled in his third touchdown in two games on a 2-yard pass from Watson on third-and-goal with 1:22 remaining.


              It was the first time since Week 13 of the 2020 season against Tennessee that the Browns scored at least 21 points in the second quarter.


              The Steelers got within 21-10 on Boswell’s 31-yard field goal with 8 seconds left before halftime.

articles.headline: Browns best Steelers on TNF to take lead in AFC North
articles.description: The Browns move to 3-1 while adding to Pittsburgh's historic five-year futility in Cleveland.
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- After losing hold of an 11-point lead in the fourth quarter, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson delivered a late-game performance again on Thursday night. Andre Szmyt made a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds and safety Grant Delpit intercepted a last-second heave from quarterback Aaron Rodgers as the Browns defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers in a 27-24 win.

The victory marks the first time the Browns have sat atop the division since Nov. 9, 2014. It's also Cleveland's first 3-1 start since the 2021 season.

After the offense struggled in the first half of the team's first three games, the unit broke out with three consecutive touchdown drives in the second quarter to give the Browns a 21-10 lead at halftime.

Cleveland's offense stalled in the second half, as Watson turned the ball over twice after halftime, but the starting QB, who entered Week 4 with two straight game-winning drives, led his third of the young season.

Watson completed 24 of 33 passes for 268 yards with one touchdown and an interception. He also ran for 22 yards on seven carries and lost a fumble.

After running for a combined 131 yards in the season's first two games, the Browns ran for 112 yards on Thursday night, the second time the team has had back-to-back 100-yard rushing efforts.

Cleveland's defense sacked Rodgers five times and intercepted him twice.

Cleveland Browns (3-1)

What to make of the QB performance: Watson started off strong before cooling off in the second half and turning it on late again. Watson's 181 passing yards were the most he has thrown for in the first half of a game with the Steelers, but his two turnovers after halftime helped Pittsburgh erase the deficit. Watson, though, was clutch for the third straight game, building on his early-season momentum.

Stat to know: The Browns scored 21 points in the first half, their most in any half of a game since Week 8 of the 2024 season, when Cleveland scored 23 points against the Baltimore Ravens in the second half.

Trend to watch: Cleveland was flagged for 17 total penalties, the second straight game with at least 14 infractions. Entering Week 4, the Browns had been called for the second-most penalties in the NFL (34). -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: Oct. 11 at New York Jets

Pittsburgh Steelers (2-2)

Meetings between the Steelers and Browns in Cleveland are always weird, but Thursday night just as it has been for the past five years, it ended the same way: with a Pittsburgh loss.

This time around, the Steelers rallied to erase a 14-point deficit -- the byproduct of a catastrophic second quarter -- with a vintage Rodgers drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter that featured two completions of 20-plus yards to wide receiver DK Metcalf and a quarterback sneak for a successful two-point conversion. But in the final 1:42, the Browns moved down the field by picking on a Steelers secondary down its top two cornerbacks.

articles.description: Cleveland Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday night's home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers because of a knee injury.
articles.headlineJa: ブラウンズのDTメイソン・グラハム、膝の負傷で試合を途中退場
articles.descriptionJa: クリーブランド・ブラウンズのディフェンシブタックル（DT）メイソン・グラハムは、膝の負傷のため木曜夜のピッツバーグ・スティーラーズ戦の残り時間を欠場することが決定した。
articles.body:
CLEVELAND -- Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham was ruled out for the remainder of Thursday night's 27-24 home win over the Pittsburgh Steelers because of a knee injury.

Graham sustained the injury during Pittsburgh's opening series, as his left leg bent awkwardly while he was being blocked. Graham walked to the medical tent with some assistance before walking to the locker room.

The No. 5 pick in the 2025 draft, Graham is off to a strong start to his second season. His four sacks lead the Browns and are tied for the second most in the NFL.

The Browns' defensive line depth took another hit later when Mike Hall Jr., Graham's replacement, was carted to the locker room because of an ankle injury he sustained in the second quarter. Hall returned in the third quarter.

articles.headline: Jalen Duren accepts 5-year, $200M deal from Pistons
articles.description: Jalen Duren agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Pistons, agent Chafie Fields told ESPN's Shams Charania ahead of a Thursday night deadline the All-NBA center had to accept a 1-year qualifying offer.
articles.headlineJa: ジェーレン・デューレン、ピストンズからの5年2億ドルの契約を受け入れ
articles.descriptionJa: オールNBAセンターのジェーレン・デューレンが、5年総額2億ドルの完全保証契約でピストンズに残留することに合意した。代理人のチャフィー・フィールズ氏がESPNのシャムズ・シャラニア記者に明かした。この合意は、デューレンが1年のクオリファイング・オファーを受け入れる木曜夜の期限前に行われた。
articles.body:
All-NBA center Jalen Duren agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, agent Chafie Fields of THE•TEAM told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday night.

The agreement ends a four-month contract standoff between the sides that spanned throughout the summer and continued into the start of training camp this week.

Duren, a restricted free agent, remained unsigned at the beginning of camp, skipping media day and sat out the first few practices of the year after he did not initially accept a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract offer from the team two weeks ago. He previously had offers ranging from $170 million to $190 million throughout the summer, according to Charania. 

But Duren ultimately accepted the standing Pistons proposal, doing so ahead of an 11.59 p.m. ET deadline Thursday that he had to accept a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer from Detroit, which would have made him an unrestricted free agent next summer. However, such a deal would have been unprecedented for a player of his caliber; no player who has made an All-NBA or All-Star team has signed a qualifying offer.

Duren's issue went beyond the money, however.

Sources told Charania earlier this week that his representatives made it clear that he felt disrespected by the process, especially compared with how the team handled the contract extension of forward Ausar Thompson, who agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale deal with the Pistons earlier this month. Duren also took issue with weight clauses in some of the team's previous offers.

Duren, 22, is coming off the best regular season in his young career. He averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds on 65% shooting in 70 games while helping the Pistons secure the No.1 seed in the Eastern Conference. But his production drastically dropped in the postseason, where he averaged 10.5 points and 8.5 rebounds on 51% shooting in 14 games as Detroit was eliminated by the Cleveland Cavaliers in Game 7 of the East semifinals.

Throughout his playoff struggles and as the standoff continued during the summer, the Pistons have insisted that Duren was a major part of the team's future, refusing to engage with potential sign-and-trade proposals.

President of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said he still had confidence Duren would return to the team on some sort of deal. Coach J.B. Bickerstaff and star Cade Cunningham threw their support to Duren during the team's media day and said they kept in contact with him throughout the summer.

The Pistons will play their first preseason game Monday, when they host the Phoenix Suns.

The other 28 teams in the association joined them Monday, ahead of training camps beginning for most teams.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first media day away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their first impressions?

Oct. 1

Duren, Pistons end standoff with long-term deal

All-NBA center Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, his agent told ESPN's Shams Charania. Duren had until 11:59 p.m. ET Thursday to decide on the Pistons' one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer.

Mitch Johnson excited about Billy Donovan's role with Spurs

San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson likes what he's seen so far at training camp from new lead assistant coach Billy Donovan.

"I don't want to be naive enough to think I'm going to tell you what a 61-year old Hall of Fame coach like Billy Donovan and his resume can bring to the table," Johnson said. "I'm excited he's here. He's a tremendous person, great personality, fits in seamlessly. He's got worlds of experience and he's an extremely hard worker. He's not kicking up his feet and telling stories. He's rolling his sleeves up and getting his hands dirty. He's going to help all of us and probably me, specifically, a ton this year."

Donovan joined the staff in July, replacing former lead assistant Sean Sweeney, who left San Antonio to take the head coaching job in Orlando. Sweeney ran the Spurs' defense last season, helping it improve from 25th to third in the NBA in defensive rating (110.4).

Donovan won't be tasked with taking on Sweeney's responsibilities, according to sources, however. San Antonio brought in Donovan to lean on his experience on both ends of the floor, as well as his vast knowledge of the NBA and college games.

A member of the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame class of 2025, Donovan joined the Spurs after 11 seasons as an NBA coach with the Chicago Bulls and Oklahoma City Thunder, after capturing two college basketball national titles in 2006 and 2007 with the Florida Gators. -- Michael C. Wright

articles.headlineJa: 2026年NBAフリーエージェンシー：オフシーズンの契約と契約延長の評価
articles.descriptionJa: ステフの新たな2年契約をはじめ、主要なフリーエージェント契約や契約延長の採点・評価を行っています。
articles.body:
The NBA offseason is here, and teams across the league have been busy making moves. Free agency officially began June 30.

I'm grading every free agent signing and the most impactful extensions this offseason, breaking down the ramifications for all teams and players involved.

To determine each grade, I'm looking at multiple factors, including the player's on-court impact and age, the contract's financial implications and the context of the team's short- and long-term outlooks. How risky or certain is the move? And how much does it help or hurt the team's chance to win a championship, next season or beyond?

Let's get into the latest moves:

Quick links: 

Trade grades | Latest buzz | Trade machine

Depth charts | Trade tracker | More coverage

Oct. 1: Duren signs five-year deal with Pistons

Jalen Duren terms: Five years, $200 million

Grade: B

Your opinion of Duren's new contract rests on one key question: How severely do you penalize him for one bad postseason?

At the end of the regular season, Duren seemed like a shoo-in to receive at least a $200 million deal. He was a deserving All-Star and All-NBA third team honoree, averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game. He helped lead the Pistons to 60 wins and the East's No. 1 seed. His 69% true shooting mark was by far the best in NBA history for a player with an above-average usage rate.

And Duren even played well without Cade Cunningham, showing that the center's production was not solely a product of his point guard's brilliance. The Pistons had a plus-11.5 net rating when Duren played without Cunningham, per databallr, as well as a plus-11.5 net rating when the two played together. Detroit's net rating fell to plus-7.6 when Cunningham played without Duren.

But then came the playoffs, and Duren looked like a completely different player: Less confident, less assertive, less impactful. This wasn't a matter of one bad game or one tricky matchup; rather, he struggled across 14 games, against two very different opponents.

Compared to the regular season, Duren averaged 9.3 fewer points per game in the playoffs. That's the largest drop for an All-Star since 1969 (minimum 10 games), per ESPN Research. And his player efficiency rating dropped from 26.1 in the regular season (sixth-best in the NBA) to a below-average 13.8 in the playoffs. That's also the biggest drop for an All-Star in playoff history.

For a player of that caliber, $40 million per year seems like an overpay.

That uncertainty following his playoff shortcoming makes this deal a clear choice for Duren, even if he waited until the restricted free agency qualifying offer deadline to sign it. According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, even if Duren had received a max contract next summer after playing on the one-year qualifying offer in 2026-27, he would have received a maximum of $198.8 million over the next five years.

articles.headline: 76ers envision LeBron James' role being 'offense creator'
articles.description: Sixers coach Nick Nurse envisions LeBron James setting the table for the offense this season. "I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said.
articles.headlineJa: 76ers、レブロン・ジェームズの役割を「オフェンスの創造者」と構想
articles.descriptionJa: シクサーズのニック・ナースHCは、今季レブロン・ジェームズがお膳立て役を担うことを見込んでいます。「私は彼を素晴らしいオフェンスの創造者だと考えている」とナースHCは語りました。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- It took until Day 3 of training camp for Philadelphia 76ers coach Nick Nurse to introduce offensive schemes to his new group.

And though the offense flowed with expected ease Thursday during 5-on-0 drills, role definition will be as important as understanding the playbook when the real games start.

Nurse detailed the offensive responsibilities he envisions LeBron James occupying. The team will certainly put the ball in the 24-year veteran's capable hands -- as, team sources told ESPN, Philadelphia discussed playing James at point forward this offseason -- but he won't be the only one with the ball.

"We got several guys that what I would call 'grab-and-go,'" Nurse said. "If they get rebounds and their first advantage is to start pushing it up the floor and it stays that way, then they're going to do it."

Beyond James, the group Nurse will rely on to push the team in transition includes fellow starters Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and VJ Edgecombe.

Though Nurse emphasized defense during the first two days of camp, part of the presentation was imploring his players to get stops to spark fast-break opportunities when scoring will come instinctively.

When the Sixers set up in the half court, however, Nurse is glad to have James, who ranks No. 1 in all-time points and No. 4 in all-time assists on this team.

"I just think LeBron, I consider him a great offense creator," Nurse said. "I don't necessarily mean scorer, I just think creator and a table setter and all that kind of stuff. ... If it isn't bringing it up and starting [the possession], it's probably going to be first pass anyway to [him on] the wing and then we get into our actions, and he's kind of seeing what's there, and he's creating offense for others."

As the Sixers look to organize themselves against a set defense, that's when player recognition will be paramount.

James, Brown and Joel Embiid, for instance, can operate out of the post to initiate offense. The court, however, can get awfully crowded if the team has a player planted on either block and any of those three expect their touches there.

"One, it's a feel thing, and two, we just try to establish some spacing," Brown said. "We try to establish position on the floor, like the style of play. I think we're still kind of figuring it out. Like when I am going to go, when not to go, when big fella is going down in the post, when I can put pressure on the rim, just trying to find that balance."

Brown has already spent time with coaches after practice this week, not only practicing fadeaway shots when double-teamed in the post, but also practicing throwing passes to the 3-point line to elude the double.

Sixers player development coaches have been the recipients of those passes, but the idea is for Brown to picture finding one of his star teammates open if he dissects the defense properly.

"I played with a fair share of stretch 5s, and it really complements my game well," Brown said of Embiid.

articles.headline: Falcons and Saints renew their longstanding rivalry as each seek early season momentum
articles.description: — Long-time Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan can be counted on to echo the sentiments of many New Orleans fans whenever the rival Atlanta Falcons are next on the schedule.
articles.headlineJa: ファルコンズとセインツ、シーズン序盤の弾みをつけるべく長年のライバル対決へ
articles.descriptionJa: セインツで長年活躍するディフェンシブエンド（DE）キャメロン・ジョーダンは、ライバルのアトランタ・ファルコンズとの試合が近づくたび、ニューオーリンズの多くのファンの思いを代弁してくれる。
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- — Long-time Saints defensive end Cameron Jordan can be counted on to echo the sentiments of many New Orleans fans whenever the rival Atlanta Falcons are next on the schedule. 


              “You know the importance of this game," Jordan said, referring to the Falcons' visit to New Orleans on Monday night. “‘Can’tlanta’ comes to the dome. We have to turn them into ‘Trashlanta.'”


              The Falcons (1-2) and Saints (1-2) have identical records, but New Orleans has played close in all three of its games, while Atlanta has been more erratic.


              After being booed by their own fans during a 34-3 home loss to Carolina in Week 2, the Falcons stunningly routed the Packers in Green Bay just four days later.


              They'll have had 10 days rest when they enter the hostile, emotionally charged Superdome on what is also being celebrated as the 20-year anniversary of when the Saints played their first game in the rebuilt stadium since it had been damaged while sheltering desperate residents during Hurricane Katrina. 


              That also was a Monday night game against the Falcons. It started with Steve Gleason's famous punt block and ended with the city celebrating a 23-3 Saints triumph.


              “That’s the fun part for us,” Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said. “In this league, you go on the road; you get to experience some incredible crowds.” 


              Stefanski takes confidence from how well Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and his offense handled Green Bay's crowd, not committing one pre-snap penalty.


              “That’s no small feat ... in some of these road environments,” Stefanski said. “Mike did an outstanding job both in the huddle and at the line of scrimmage the other night, and getting us in and out of the correct plays, making adjustments when necessary.”


              The result was a number of impressive statistical lines for Penix (256 yards passing), running back Bijan Robinson (194 yards, two TDs rushing) and receiver Drake London (nine catches for 194 yards).


              Last week, the Saints looked to be on their way to a victory that would have given them an early edge in the NFC South race, only to squander an 11-point, second-half lead to the Las Vegas Raiders, committing four turnovers in the process.


              “We've only played three games. It's nothing to panic over," Saints tight end Juwan Johnson said. “We're playing really aggressive, really strong, really physical, really smart and really fast. There's just a few things we can clean up and we'll be fine.” 


              In New Orleans, a city oozing with mysticism, there are bound to be more than a few rituals, superstitious or otherwise, practiced up to and during the game.


              Stefanski, though, sounds intent to just focus on the game plan.


              “I’m not superstitious,” Stefanski said. “It’s bad luck.”

articles.headlineJa: スペインのビクトル・ムニョス、リヴァプール移籍について語る：プレミアリーグはラ・リーガよりもフィジカル的だ
articles.descriptionJa: 今夏ラ・リーガから移籍して以来、リヴァプールのウィングであるビクトル・ムニョスはプレミアリーグのクラブの「インテンシティ」を称賛し、この環境の変化が選手としての「成長に役立っている」と語りました。
